body.heading: Where in the world is Zambia?
paragraphs: Zambia is a country in Eastern Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Zambia is Lusaka.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Zambia is English.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Zambia is the Zambian kwacha.

body.heading: How big is Zambia?
paragraphs: Zambia covers about 753,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about three times the size of Guinea.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: The Zambezi River plunges over a mile-wide cliff at Victoria Falls — 'the Smoke that Thunders' — sending up rainbows and clouds of spray you can see for miles.
South Luangwa is famous for walking safaris and leopards — expert guides lead families on foot among giraffes, elephants and hippos along the Luangwa River.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Zambia on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Zambia in one breath: a country in Eastern Africa, capital Lusaka, where people speak English and pay with the Zambian kwacha.
